source_text_cells.source_text: Seabirds Count Dataset: Seabirds Count – Seabird 2000 comparative data

This workbook contains the totalled adjusted count of each species in Seabird 2000 and Seabirds Count per breeding site. 
The workbook consists of 4 worksheets: this coversheet, and three worksheets containing data. Worksheet 1 contains the full dataset (totalled adjusted count of each species in Seabird 2000 and Seabirds Count per breeding site); Worksheet 2 contains the complete Atlantic Puffin dataset; Worksheet 3 contains the comparable Atlantic Pfuffin dataset.

When using the data please cite: Burnell, D., Perkins, A.J., Newton, S.F., Bolton, M., Tierney, T.D. & Dunn, T.E., 2023. Seabirds Count: a census of breeding seabirds in Britain and Ireland (2015–2021). Lynx Nature Books, Barcelona.

1. Where NA is given, this means there were no data available at the time of the analysis to produce a comparison. 
2. The Lesser Black-backed and Herring Gull data in this dataset is for natural nest sites only, this does no include the 1 km urban square data.
3. For Northern Gannet, the previous censuses data is from the 2003-05 Gannet census not Seabird 2000.
4. Data for Atlantic Puffin are separated out into two separate worksheets: Worksheet 2 is the complete dataset (where all data from both censuses is present, regardless of comparability); Worksheet 3 is the comparable dataset (where only data from records with suitably comparable methods and timings between the two censuses are present). 
5. Since the publication of Seabird 2000, new data have emerged or ammendments to the original data have occurred, therefore there are likely to be differences in the totals of countries/counties/administrations compared to those given in Mitchell et al 2004.

Some species have been omitted from this dataset as they are regarded as confidential species these are: Little Tern, Roseate Tern and Mediterranean Gull. The datasets for these species are only available by request to seabirdscountcoordinator@jncc.gov.uk

AON: Apparently Occupied Nest
AOS: Apparently Occupied Site
AOT: Apparently Occupied Territory
AOB: Apparently Occupied Burrow
IND: Individual adults
Please note that this version was published in July 2024. This version supersedes any earlier copies of this dataset (published in November 2023 and December 2023), which contained some minor errors.
